nodes.name: Functions
nodes.description: Reusable named blocks of code that take inputs and produce outputs, letting programs be organised into smaller, composable, repeatable pieces.

nodes.name: Events
nodes.description: Programming constructs that respond to occurrences such as user input or messages, central to event-driven environments like Scratch.

nodes.name: Conditionals
nodes.description: Conditional statements that execute different code branches depending on whether a boolean expression evaluates to true or false.

nodes.name: Control Flow and C Foundations
nodes.name_zh: 控制流与 C 语言基础

nodes.name: Loops
nodes.description: Control structures that repeat a block of code, either a fixed number of times or while a condition holds, to automate repetition.

nodes.name: Abstraction
nodes.description: Hiding implementation detail behind simpler interfaces so complex systems can be built and reasoned about in manageable layers.

nodes.name: C Syntax
nodes.description: The grammatical rules of the C language governing how statements, expressions, and declarations are written so the compiler can interpret them.

nodes.name: Data Types
nodes.description: Categories such as int, char, float, and double specifying how values are stored, their size in memory, and the operations allowed on them.

nodes.name: Operators
nodes.description: Symbols performing computations on values, including arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators, combined to form expressions.

nodes.name: Compilation Process
nodes.description: The process translating C source code into an executable through preprocessing, compiling, assembling, and linking stages.

nodes.name: Debugging
nodes.description: The systematic process of locating and fixing program defects using tools, print statements, and reasoning about expected versus actual behaviour.

nodes.name: Arrays
nodes.description: Contiguous, fixed-size collections of same-typed elements accessed by integer index in constant time, the basis of many data structures.

nodes.name: Strings
nodes.description: Sequences of characters represented in C as null-terminated arrays of chars, manipulated through library functions and pointer operations.

nodes.name: Command-line Arguments
nodes.description: Arguments passed to a program at launch, received through argc and argv, letting users configure behaviour from the command line.

nodes.name: Linear Search
nodes.description: A search algorithm scanning elements one by one until the target is found or the collection is exhausted, running in linear time.
nodes.visual_hint: Scan an array element by element highlighting the comparison until found.

nodes.name: Binary Search
nodes.description: An efficient search on sorted data that repeatedly halves the search interval by comparing the target to the middle element, running in logarithmic time.
nodes.visual_hint: Halve a sorted array each step, narrowing the search interval.

nodes.name: Sorting Algorithms
nodes.description: Algorithms arranging elements into order, such as bubble, selection, and merge sort, differing in strategy and time complexity.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate bubble, selection, and merge sort rearranging an array.

nodes.name: Recursion
nodes.description: A technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller subproblems, combining base and recursive cases to terminate.
nodes.visual_hint: Step recursive calls building up and unwinding on the call stack.

nodes.name: Big O Notation
nodes.description: Big O notation describing how an algorithm's running time or space grows with input size, characterising worst-case asymptotic efficiency.
nodes.visual_hint: Plot growth of constant, log, linear, n-log-n, and quadratic complexity.

nodes.name: Pointers
nodes.description: Variables storing memory addresses, enabling indirect access, dynamic data structures, and efficient passing of data by reference in C.
nodes.visual_hint: Box-and-pointer diagram of variables holding memory addresses.

nodes.name: Dynamic Memory Allocation
nodes.description: Dynamic memory allocation requesting heap memory at run time with malloc and releasing it with free, enabling data sized during execution.

nodes.name: Call Stack
nodes.description: The region of memory tracking active function calls, storing each call's local variables, parameters, and return address in stack frames.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram stack frames pushed and popped as functions are called.

nodes.name: File I/O
nodes.description: Reading from and writing to files using library functions, enabling programs to persist and retrieve data beyond their execution.

nodes.name: Linked Lists
nodes.description: A dynamic data structure of nodes each holding data and a pointer to the next, allowing efficient insertion and deletion without contiguous memory.
nodes.visual_hint: Box-and-pointer chain of nodes linked by next pointers.

nodes.name: Hash Tables
nodes.description: A structure mapping keys to values using a hash function to index into buckets, giving average constant-time insertion and lookup.
nodes.visual_hint: Hash keys into buckets and resolve a collision.

nodes.name: Trees
nodes.description: Hierarchical data structures of nodes linked from a root, such as binary search trees, enabling efficient ordered storage and lookup.
nodes.visual_hint: Insert and search nodes in a binary search tree.

nodes.name: Tries
nodes.description: Tree structures indexing strings by their characters along paths, enabling fast prefix-based search and autocomplete at the cost of memory.

nodes.name: Queues and Stacks
nodes.description: Two abstract data types: stacks following last-in-first-out order and queues following first-in-first-out order, for managing ordered access.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate push/pop on a stack and enqueue/dequeue on a queue.

nodes.name: Python Syntax
nodes.description: The readable, indentation-based syntax of Python, a high-level interpreted language emphasising concise expression of common programming constructs.

nodes.name: Lists and Dictionaries
nodes.description: Python's core collections: ordered, mutable lists and dictionaries mapping keys to values, supporting flexible data manipulation.

nodes.name: Object-Oriented Programming
nodes.description: Object-oriented programming in Python organising code into classes that bundle data and methods, supporting encapsulation, inheritance, and reuse.

nodes.name: Exceptions
nodes.description: Python's mechanism for handling run-time errors by raising and catching exceptions with try-except blocks, separating error handling from normal logic.

nodes.name: Relational Databases
nodes.description: Databases storing data in related tables of rows and columns, with keys linking tables, managed through a relational database system.

nodes.name: SQL Queries
nodes.description: SQL statements that retrieve and modify data in relational tables, expressing selection, filtering, and ordering declaratively.

nodes.name: SQL Joins
nodes.description: SQL joins combining rows from multiple tables based on related columns, enabling queries that span relationships between tables.

nodes.name: SQL Indexes
nodes.description: Database indexes, auxiliary structures that speed up lookups on chosen columns at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.

nodes.name: HTML
nodes.description: HyperText Markup Language defining the structure and content of web pages through nested, semantic tags rendered by browsers.

nodes.name: CSS
nodes.description: Cascading Style Sheets controlling the visual presentation of HTML, including layout, colours, fonts, and responsive design via rules.

nodes.name: JavaScript
nodes.description: JavaScript, the browser's programming language adding interactivity and dynamic behaviour to web pages through an event-driven model.

nodes.name: DOM Manipulation
nodes.description: The Document Object Model, a tree representation of a web page that JavaScript can read and modify to update content dynamically.
nodes.visual_hint: Tree diagram of the DOM nodes of a web page.

nodes.name: HTTP Protocol
nodes.description: The HyperText Transfer Protocol governing request-response communication between web clients and servers using methods and status codes.

nodes.name: Flask Framework
nodes.description: Flask, a lightweight Python web framework for building web applications and APIs by mapping URL routes to handler functions.

nodes.name: MVC Architecture
nodes.description: The Model-View-Controller pattern separating data, presentation, and control logic to organise web application code cleanly.

nodes.name: Sessions and Cookies
nodes.description: Sessions and cookies maintaining state across stateless HTTP requests, identifying users and remembering data between page visits.

nodes.name: APIs
nodes.description: Application programming interfaces exposing functionality and data over the web, commonly returning JSON for other programs to consume.

nodes.name: Cybersecurity Basics
nodes.description: The practice of protecting systems, networks, and data from attack, covering the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.

nodes.name: Encryption
nodes.description: Transforming data into ciphertext using algorithms and keys so that only authorised parties can read it, underpinning secure communication.

nodes.name: Authentication
nodes.description: Verifying the identity of a user or system, typically through passwords, tokens, or biometrics, before granting access to resources.

nodes.name: Vulnerabilities
nodes.description: Weaknesses in software or systems that attackers can exploit, such as injection or buffer overflows, requiring mitigation and patching.
